Star 1 has [Fe/H] = 0 and [Si/Fe] = 0.3, so [Si/H] = [Si/Fe] + [Fe/H] = 0.3. Thus the silicon abundance relative to hydrogen in Star 1 is 10^0.3 times solar.

Star 2 has [Mg/H] = 0 and [Mg/Si] = 0.3. Since [Mg/Si] = log(nMg/nSi)_star - log(nMg/nSi)_sun = 0.3, then (nMg/nSi)_star = 10^0.3 (nMg/nSi)_sun. With (nMg/nH)_star = (nMg/nH)_sun, we find (nSi/nH)_star = (nSi/nMg)_star (nMg/nH)_star = (1/10^0.3)(nSi/nMg)_sun (nMg/nH)_sun = 10^{-0.3} (nSi/nH)_sun. So [Si/H]_2 = -0.3.

The ratio of silicon atoms in the photospheres (assuming comparable hydrogen content) is therefore 10^0.3 / 10^{-0.3} = 10^{0.6} ≈ 3.98, which matches option D.

Answer: D

We have:
For Star1: [Si/Fe]_1 = 0.3 dex. [Fe/H]_1 = 0 dex.
Definition: [Si/Fe] = log10(nSi/nFe)_star - log10(nSi/nFe)_sun. So [Si/Fe]_1 = 0.3 => (nSi/nFe)_star1 / (nSi/nFe)_sun = 10^{0.3} ≈ 2.0 (since 10^{0.3}=1.9953). Also [Fe/H]_1 = 0 => (nFe/nH)_star1 / (nFe/nH)_sun = 1. So (nFe/nH)_star1 = (nFe/nH)_sun. So then (nSi/nH)_star1 = (nSi/nFe)_star1 * (nFe/nH)_star1 = (10^{0.3} * (nSi/nFe)_sun) * (nFe/nH)_sun = 10^{0.3} * (nSi/nH)_sun. So [Si/H]_1 = [Si/Fe]_1 + [Fe/H]_1 = 0.3 + 0 = 0.3 dex. So nSi/nH for Star1 is 10^{0.3} times solar.

Now for Star2: We have [Mg/Si]_2 = 0.3 dex and [Mg/H]_2 = 0 dex.
[Mg/Si] = log10(nMg/nSi)_star - log10(nMg/nSi)_sun = 0.3 => (nMg/nSi)_star2 = 10^{0.3} * (nMg/nSi)_sun.
[Mg/H]_2 = 0 => (nMg/nH)_star2 = (nMg/nH)_sun.
Then (nSi/nH)_star2 = (nSi/nMg)_star2 * (nMg/nH)_star2. But (nSi/nMg)_star2 = 1 / (nMg/nSi)_star2 = 1/(10^{0.3} (nMg/nSi)_sun) = (1/10^{0.3}) * (nSi/nMg)_sun. So (nSi/nH)_star2 = (1/10^{0.3}) * (nSi/nMg)_sun * (nMg/nH)_sun = (1/10^{0.3}) * (nSi/nH)_sun. Because (nSi/nMg)_sun * (nMg/nH)_sun = (nSi/nH)_sun. So [Si/H]_2 = -0.3 dex. So Star2 has Si/H = 10^{-0.3} times solar.

Thus ratio of Si atoms (assuming H abundance same) = (nSi/nH)_star1 / (nSi/nH)_star2 = 10^{0.3} / 10^{-0.3} = 10^{0.6} ≈ 3.981. So about 3.98. That matches option (D) ~3.9.

Thus answer is D.
